## Design

### 2026-11-08: So I haven't touched digital logic in a year and might've forgotten some stuff so I started out by messing around with the Circuitverse website and options the website provides to get a feel for it (p

**9h**

So I haven't touched digital logic in a year and might've forgotten some stuff so I started out by messing around with the Circuitverse website and options the website provides to get a feel for it (personally think this website sucks honestly but It'll  probably be fine) This was after a little research on which would be the most suitable for this project. I ended up not wanting to go through the trouble of downloading something on linux.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/b9c87334c9c2c24d016945043286481b56e34a4eed08a754fed59d80825b67d7.png)
I always wondered how people make calculators and such in Minecraft and Build a Boat for Treasure so I ended up wanting to do something like this for the custom project week.
Following a tutorial, it ended up being easier than I thought (I've already derived all the gates from flip flops before in the past so I didn't start there). Most of it was more fighting with the website honestly.
After a bit, I made a 3-bit adder (significant bits on the right). This is 6+5=11:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/60b1ad8efacf11b59c418d34d297fd0a32e1229e3c79be216a64c2545fec31cc.png)

And 4+5=9:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/bd2867c9daf31fce00b7c63d2ddffc69d0387a29bc5d8495085fd9575c4f7b70.png)

But I quickly realized that this wasn't scalable and quickly deleted everything to make it purely a 1-bit adder and modular. I also became antsy about how it wasn't significant bits on the left for some reason so I made it so. The C_in is so that the other 1-bit adders are able to send overflowing bits up, pretty cool ig (1+1+1=3):
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/583a591b2e4f3da31ceb0720847ec7338e015824a184ba6a410804dfad53005e.png)

From here on out it was pretty easy, I just combined all the 1-bit adders together and made a 4-bit adder (2+1=3):
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/17d173aea82ccf7403020b8aa1df6f053a599b73cec55ac368b8811745aceef8.png)

A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/14f90b53daf52c46cdac7d20525e86434b9937138d4f89596d6da12fbe49879b.png)

I realized I would have a much easier time with the rest of the project if I made the input and outputs a big binary buffer instead of having a bajillion input pins. Also here's 15+7=22:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/17d173aea82ccf7403020b8aa1df6f053a599b73cec55ac368b8811745aceef8.png)

And bam we got a 16-bit calculator just like that by combining 4 of the 4-bit adders (8,869+8,815=17,684):
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/1a3c91a6f1180a25f8c40b36a3cec2f6e84f8f8544795d9104c83cfcd51cfda7.png)

Okay but now we need to deal with the subtraction and thankfully I already knew about 2's complement and how it works so I quickly made a submodule for that:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/5f11ed1b3b7096032fa9cd86f5dccfb7699e5b7c5b0188c22bd8594b935caf59.png)

And thus we have a 16-bit subtractor by adding input A with the 2's complement of B (3-2=1):
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/1f8e4123514355e2af1f8692de843ead41a11866d60ad7f33e01898fb044afc3.png)

 Also very interesting how it works out of the box if you subtract 1 from  0 (2's complement representation of  -1):
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/7b046fdb5e525dd84416a67e62a4dd06e25faa7e86e37d38c4676f22d20b514e.png)
